3	Scope: 2H-WS2. Numbers appear only where they were read in the cited source; the locator says where.
4	"Consensus" means several independent sources agree; "single source" means one paper. The defining practical

8	- Bulk D6h zone-centre modes A1g + 2A2u + 2B2g + B1u + E1g + 2E1u + 2E2g + E2u; A1g, E1g, E2g Raman active,
9	  E1g forbidden in backscattering (Hait S. et al. 2022, J. Appl. Phys. 132, 133901, doi:10.1063/5.0107655,
10	  p.4). 1L is D3h (E2g1 to E', A1g to A1'), odd N D3h, even N D3d (Yang J. et al. 2017, arXiv:1706.01677, p.5).
11	- At 514.5 nm, 1L: 2LA(M) 351.1, E2g1 355.2, A1g 417.2 cm-1; bulk 350.0, 355.3, 420.1; LA(M) near 176 at 488 nm
12	  (Berkdemir A. et al. 2013, Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, Table 1).
13	- Resonant 1L spectrum also contains bands at 176, 193, 231, 353 (2LA), 583 and 702 (4LA) cm-1, all zone-edge
14	  combinations (Zhang X. et al. 2015, Chem. Soc. Rev. 44, 2757, arXiv:1502.00701, p.14, Fig. 11c, Table III).
15	
16	## Thickness
17	- A1g stiffens with N (417.2, 418.4, 419.0, 420.1 cm-1 for 1L, 2L, 3L, bulk at 514.5 nm) while E2g1 barely moves
18	  (Berkdemir 2013, Table 1). Consensus on the trend. So the A1g-E2g1 separation grows only a few cm-1.
19	- The A1g-E2g1 separation: about 62 cm-1 in 1L to 66 in bulk, as relayed by Mitioglu A. A. et al. 2014,
20	  PRB 89, 245442, arXiv:1406.3511, p.2.
21	- 1L flags at resonance: 2LA(M)/A1g intensity ratio about 2 at 514 nm, decreasing with N (Berkdemir 2013).
22	  The ratio depends on polarization (see below), so use it only with known polarization.
23	- A peak near 310 cm-1 is present in multilayers and absent in 1L (Zhao W. et al. 2013, Nanoscale 5, 9677,
24	  arXiv:1304.0911, p.10, Fig. 5b). Assignment unclear in that paper (proposed shear-related combination).
25	- Low-frequency shear and breathing series determine N (Yang 2017, abstract). At A-exciton resonance the
26	  Raman-forbidden lowest shear mode of odd N appears as strong as the allowed even-N one, with a Fano line shape
27	  (Yang 2017, abstract): do not use its presence as a parity test at that laser.
28	
29	## Strain and doping
30	- Uniaxial strain on 1L WS2 redshifts the modes, in-plane modes faster, and splits E'; WS2 shows much larger
31	  changes in mode positions and intensities than WSe2 under the same strain; at large strain the polarization
32	  response of a mode changes (Dadgar A. M. et al. 2018, Chem. Mater., doi:10.1021/acs.chemmater.8b01672,
33	  arXiv:1705.05412, abstract; WS2 data Fig. 3b, calculated shifts Fig. 4c,d). Strain rates for WS2 not extracted here.
34	- Doping: no WS2-specific Raman doping rate verified. By analogy with MoS2 (Chakraborty 2012, see MoS2.md) an
35	  A1g shift with broadening would point to electron doping; this is an inference, not a WS2 measurement.
36	
37	## Defects and quality
38	- No WS2-specific defect calibration verified. LA(M) near 176 cm-1 is present already in pristine spectra near
39	  resonance (Berkdemir 2013, 488 nm), so its presence alone is not a defect marker in WS2, unlike LA(M) in
40	  off-resonant MoS2 (inference from the two sources).
41	- The band near 297 cm-1 is the backscattering-forbidden E1g, and the one near 325 cm-1 is E2g2+LA (Kumar D. et al.
42	  2019, J. Phys. Condens. Matter, doi:10.1088/1361-648X/ab3fec, arXiv:1906.10661, abstract). Hait 2022 (p.4)
43	  instead assigns about 325 cm-1 to an out-of-plane acoustic mode at M. Disputed.
44	- Phase: 1T and 1T' monolayer WS2 give different spectra and temperature behaviour (Kumar 2019, abstract).
45	
46	## Temperature and heating
47	- Supported 1L WS2: temperature evolution of first-order and combination modes is anomalous, attributed to
48	  detuning of the resonance and to strain from substrate thermal-expansion mismatch; some combination modes
49	  disappear (Kumar 2019, abstract). Nonlinear shifts in supported WS2 were also noted by Taube A. et al. 2014,
50	  ACS AMI, doi:10.1021/am502359k, p.5.
51	- Consequence: temperature changes intensities (resonance) as well as positions; a laser-heating estimate from
52	  peak positions needs a coefficient measured on the same substrate. No WS2 coefficient verified here.
53	
54	## Excitation wavelength and resonance
55	- 2LA(M) lies about 4 to 5 cm-1 below E2g1 and becomes stronger than the main peaks for 1.96, 2.33 and 2.41 eV
56	  (A and B exciton resonance) (Yang 2017, p.5; Mitioglu 2014, abstract). Consensus.
57	- E2g1 is enhanced near the C exciton; A1g resonates with A, B and C (Yang 2017, p.5).
58	- Bulk resonance spans 1.96 to 2.41 eV because of the broad B exciton (Zhang X. 2015, p.13). 633 nm is resonant
59	  with the A exciton of WS2 (Zhao 2013, p.9).
60	- Peaks X1 and X2, independent of thickness, appear near exciton resonances; X1 vanishes in cross polarization,
61	  X2 does not (Yang 2017, abstract). Unassigned.
62	
63	## Polarization and substrate
64	- 2LA intensity is minimal when excitation and detection are orthogonal and exceeds E2g1 in parallel; A1g behaves
65	  similarly, E2g1 is isotropic (Mitioglu 2014, p.4, Fig. 3; Yang 2017, p.5). Measure in cross polarization to
66	  isolate E2g1 (Yang 2017, p.5). Consensus.
67	- Substrate interference changes absolute and relative intensities; Yang 2017 corrects for it (p.4). Substrate
68	  strain enters through thermal-expansion mismatch (Kumar 2019).
69	
70	## Pitfalls and artifacts
71	- Fitting a single Lorentzian to the 2LA/E2g1 doublet misplaces E2g1 and can give a wrong layer number
72	  (Mitioglu 2014, abstract). Always fit both, constrained by polarization data when possible.
73	- Reported 1L positions differ between groups (Hait 2022, p.4: 2LA 353.98, E2g 357.97, A1g 418.23 cm-1;
74	  Berkdemir 2013: 351.1, 355.2, 417.2) partly from fitting model and calibration; compare to the same source.
75	- Intensity ratios are only comparable at the same laser line, polarization and substrate.
76	
77	## What to ask
78	- Laser line (resonance changes the spectrum completely), power and spot size.
79	- Polarization: unpolarized, parallel or crossed; analyser present?
80	- Substrate and oxide thickness; CVD or exfoliated; transferred; encapsulated.
81	- Measurement temperature; phase (2H vs 1T or 1T') if chemically processed.
82	- Fit model used for the 350 cm-1 region.
83	
84	## Reference figures
85	- Zhao 2013, arXiv:1304.0911, Fig. 5: 1L to 5L and bulk at 532 nm, normalized to 2LA(M); 310 cm-1 band inset.
86	- Mitioglu 2014, arXiv:1406.3511, Fig. 3: 2LA/E2g1 and A1g regions vs polarization angle (1L).
87	- Yang 2017, arXiv:1706.01677, Fig. 1c,d: thickness dependence of main and weak peaks at 2.54 eV.
88	- Berkdemir 2013, Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, Fig. 3 (open access, not on arXiv): 1L to bulk at 514.5 nm.

- Uniaxial strain on 1L WS2 redshifts the modes, in-plane modes faster, and splits E'; WS2 shows much larger
  changes in mode positions and intensities than WSe2 under the same strain; at large strain the polarization
  response of a mode changes (Dadgar A. M. et al. 2018, Chem. Mater., doi:10.1021/acs.chemmater.8b01672,
  arXiv:1705.05412, abstract; WS2 data Fig. 3b, calculated shifts Fig. 4c,d). Strain rates for WS2 not extracted here.
- Doping: no WS2-specific Raman doping rate verified. By analogy with MoS2 (Chakraborty 2012, see MoS2.md) an
  A1g shift with broadening would point to electron doping; this is an inference, not a WS2 measurement.

## Defects and quality
- No WS2-specific defect calibration verified. LA(M) near 176 cm-1 is present already in pristine spectra near
  resonance (Berkdemir 2013, 488 nm), so its presence alone is not a defect marker in WS2, unlike LA(M) in
  off-resonant MoS2 (inference from the two sources).
- The band near 297 cm-1 is the backscattering-forbidden E1g, and the one near 325 cm-1 is E2g2+LA (Kumar D. et al.
  2019, J. Phys. Condens. Matter, doi:10.1088/1361-648X/ab3fec, arXiv:1906.10661, abstract). Hait 2022 (p.4)
  instead assigns about 325 cm-1 to an out-of-plane acoustic mode at M. Disputed.
- Phase: 1T and 1T' monolayer WS2 give different spectra and temperature behaviour (Kumar 2019, abstract).

## Temperature and heating
- Supported 1L WS2: temperature evolution of first-order and combination modes is anomalous, attributed to
  detuning of the resonance and to strain from substrate thermal-expansion mismatch; some combination modes
  disappear (Kumar 2019, abstract). Nonlinear shifts in supported WS2 were also noted by Taube A. et al. 2014,
  ACS AMI, doi:10.1021/am502359k, p.5.
- Consequence: temperature changes intensities (resonance) as well as positions; a laser-heating estimate from
  peak positions needs a coefficient measured on the same substrate. No WS2 coefficient verified here.

## Excitation wavelength and resonance
- 2LA(M) lies about 4 to 5 cm-1 below E2g1 and becomes stronger than the main peaks for 1.96, 2.33 and 2.41 eV
  (A and B exciton resonance) (Yang 2017, p.5; Mitioglu 2014, abstract). Consensus.
- E2g1 is enhanced near the C exciton; A1g resonates with A, B and C (Yang 2017, p.5).
- Bulk resonance spans 1.96 to 2.41 eV because of the broad B exciton (Zhang X. 2015, p.13). 633 nm is resonant
  with the A exciton of WS2 (Zhao 2013, p.9).
- Peaks X1 and X2, independent of thickness, appear near exciton resonances; X1 vanishes in cross polarization,
  X2 does not (Yang 2017, abstract). Unassigned.

## Polarization and substrate
- 2LA intensity is minimal when excitation and detection are orthogonal and exceeds E2g1 in parallel; A1g behaves
  similarly, E2g1 is isotropic (Mitioglu 2014, p.4, Fig. 3; Yang 2017, p.5). Measure in cross polarization to
  isolate E2g1 (Yang 2017, p.5). Consensus.
- Substrate interference changes absolute and relative intensities; Yang 2017 corrects for it (p.4). Substrate
  strain enters through thermal-expansion mismatch (Kumar 2019).

## Pitfalls and artifacts
- Fitting a single Lorentzian to the 2LA/E2g1 doublet misplaces E2g1 and can give a wrong layer number
  (Mitioglu 2014, abstract). Always fit both, constrained by polarization data when possible.
- Reported 1L positions differ between groups (Hait 2022, p.4: 2LA 353.98, E2g 357.97, A1g 418.23 cm-1;
  Berkdemir 2013: 351.1, 355.2, 417.2) partly from fitting model and calibration; compare to the same source.
- Intensity ratios are only comparable at the same laser line, polarization and substrate.

## What to ask
- Laser line (resonance changes the spectrum completely), power and spot size.
- Polarization: unpolarized, parallel or crossed; analyser present?
- Substrate and oxide thickness; CVD or exfoliated; transferred; encapsulated.
- Measurement temperature; phase (2H vs 1T or 1T') if chemically processed.
- Fit model used for the 350 cm-1 region.

## Reference figures
- Zhao 2013, arXiv:1304.0911, Fig. 5: 1L to 5L and bulk at 532 nm, normalized to 2LA(M); 310 cm-1 band inset.
- Mitioglu 2014, arXiv:1406.3511, Fig. 3: 2LA/E2g1 and A1g regions vs polarization angle (1L).
- Yang 2017, arXiv:1706.01677, Fig. 1c,d: thickness dependence of main and weak peaks at 2.54 eV.
- Berkdemir 2013, Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, Fig. 3 (open access, not on arXiv): 1L to bulk at 514.5 nm.

# Artifacts and red flags in Raman spectra of 2D materials

Each entry: what it looks like, how to tell it from a real band, what to do. Sources in brackets.

## Cosmic-ray spikes
- One to three pixels wide, far narrower than any phonon line at the instrument resolution, present in one
  acquisition only. Real lines have the instrument's minimum width and repeat across accumulations or angles.
- Remove before fitting (modified z-score on the first difference: Whitaker and Hayes, Chemom. Intell. Lab. Syst.
  179, 82, 2018). In an angle series, replace spike pixels from the most similar frame (Barton and Hennelly, Appl.
  Spectrosc. 73, 893, 2019). List them under artifacts, never under peaks.

## Silicon substrate
- First-order Si line near 520.7 cm-1 (a widely used calibration convention; check the offset of the fitted
  position and flag a calibration problem when it exceeds about 1 cm-1; 520 to 520.9 is reported in practice, Lee
  et al. 2010 and Castellanos-Gomez et al. 2014). Second-order Si features near 950 and 980 cm-1 (Gillet et al.
  2017, arXiv 1708.05874, Fig. 1) and a 2TA band computed near 300 cm-1 (same paper, DFPT) can be mistaken for
  sample modes. Brillouin scattering from Si gives a line near
  4.5 cm-1 in ultra-low-frequency setups (Zhang et al., PRB 87, 115413, 2013).
- Assign these as 'Si substrate'. A strong Si line with weak sample bands suggests a thin flake.

## Calibration
- First-order wavelength calibration errors of 5 to 7 cm-1 have been reported (Lee et al., Nat. Commun. 3, 1024,
  2012). Shifts of 1 to 3 cm-1 (layer number, strain, doping) are only meaningful after a calibration check.

## Background
- Broad fluorescence or photoluminescence slopes; remove with an asymmetric least-squares baseline (arPLS or
  asPLS). For broad bands (disordered carbon D and G, amorphous phases) a global baseline can eat real signal: fit
  a local linear background together with the peaks. A Breit-Wigner-Fano line shape can absorb a background slope;
  compare line shapes by BIC.

## Low-wavenumber cutoff
- Notch and edge filters block the region near the laser line (Bragg notch filters reach about 5 to 10 cm-1,
  Zhang et al. 2013). A missing shear or breathing mode below the cutoff is not evidence of absence.

## Plasma lines
- Laser plasma lines have a fixed absolute wavelength, so their Raman shift changes when the laser changes; they
  are very narrow and do not belong to the sample. Suspect them when a narrow line has no assignment.

## Laser heating
- Phonon lines soften and broaden with temperature. Graphene G shifts about -0.016 cm-1/K (Calizo et al., Nano
  Lett. 7, 2645, 2007); 1L WS2 about -0.0093 (E) and -0.0122 (A1g) cm-1/K (Huang et al., Sci. Rep. 2016);
  few-layer MoS2 about -0.013 and -0.012 cm-1/K (Sahoo et al., arXiv 1302.5865). A power series is the test.

## Substrate interference
- On SiO2/Si, absolute intensities and intensity ratios depend on oxide thickness and laser wavelength: graphene
  I(2D)/I(G) changed by almost 370 % for a 60 % change in SiO2 thickness (Yoon et al., PRB 80, 125422, 2009).
  Never read layer number from absolute intensity or from I(2D)/I(G) without the substrate stack.

## Resonance
- Near an excitonic resonance, second-order bands can exceed first-order ones. WS2 at 514 to 532 nm: 2LA(M) lies
  about 4 cm-1 below E2g and overlaps it (Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, 2013; Mitioglu et al., PRB 89,
  245442, 2014). Fit both or the E2g position and layer count are wrong.

## Saturation and clipping
- A flat-topped peak or values at the detector maximum: the peak shape and intensity are wrong; ask for a shorter
  exposure.

content.text:
I can't finish the analysis in this session, and the structured report I submitted earlier was premature. It said the fits had produced nothing, but the 638.38 nm fit has now finished.

**What is complete**
- **QC on all 12 spectra.** The Si calibration offset drifts systematically with excitation wavelength: +1.39 cm⁻¹ at 578.95 nm, +1.24 at 618.10, +0.93 at 626.90, and +0.30 at 638.38 nm. A laser-independent Si line should not do this, so the drift points to the spectrometer calibration or the acquisition chain. It needs resolving before any shift of 1 to 3 cm⁻¹ means anything.
- **Si line missing in 8 of 12 spectra.** QC did not flag it in 585.01 to 611.28 nm and 591.66 to 607.91 nm, which I have not explained.
- **Cosmic-ray spikes** cluster in narrow windows (for example 143 to 145 cm⁻¹ at 611.28 nm and 718 to 720 cm⁻¹ at 585.01 nm). That is more consistent with a detector or cluster artifact than with single cosmic rays, and it should be checked at pixel level.
- **Single-spectrum fit at 638.38 nm (complete).** It finds the A1g-like band at 418.29 ± 0.28 cm⁻¹ (FWHM 4.9 cm⁻¹), a band at 589.9 ± 0.6 cm⁻¹ (FWHM 8.9), a band at 132.0 cm⁻¹, and the Si line at 521.0 cm⁻¹. These peak heights (≈110 to 120 counts) are small relative to the ≈200-count background in that region.

**What is not complete or is in doubt**
- **No E2g1 or 2LA(M) found at 638.38 nm.** The fit reports no peak near 350 to 357 cm⁻¹, and the raw intensity between 300 and 400 cm⁻¹ shows no resolved doublet (maximum 281 counts at 359 cm⁻¹, against a background of about 200). This is either a genuinely weak E2g1/2LA response at this laser or a fit or background problem. It is the single most important thing to settle, and I have not settled it.
- **Series fit (rl_series.py with --si-correct) has produced no output.** It was launched in the background and has run past the 10-minute background limit, so it may have been stopped.
- **578.95 nm single fit has produced no output.** It is still running or has stopped.
- **Matcher, polarization classification and literature checks were not run.**

**Blocked actions**
The environment is in "don't ask" mode, which denied Monitor and PowerShell. I could not poll the background tasks or check whether the processes are alive. I did not work around this.

**What I would do next**
1. Look at `fit.png` from the 638.38 nm fit to see whether the 350 to 357 cm⁻¹ region is baseline-limited.
2. Re-run `rl_series.py` in the foreground with a split set of files, or with `run_in_background` and a longer timeout, so the 12-spectrum series finishes.
3. Confirm the spectrometer calibration. A Si-line drift of about 1 cm⁻¹ across the excitation range is itself a finding to report to the instrument owner.

**On the resonance question**
Based on the skill's WS2 notes and not yet on these fits: the sweep covers 1.94 to 2.14 eV, which spans the A-exciton region. The notes say 2LA(M) can exceed E2g1 at A/B resonance (Yang et al. 2017, arXiv:1706.01677, p.5; Mitioglu et al. 2014, arXiv:1406.3511, abstract), and that 633 nm is resonant with the A exciton (Zhao et al. 2013, arXiv:1304.0911, p.9). The 638.38 nm spectrum shows no clear 2LA/E2g1 pair, so a strong 2LA resonance is not visible there, which I cannot yet explain. I have not measured how the peaks change across the series, so I cannot yet say which electronic states drive the changes.

**Questions for you**
- Was the spectrometer recalibrated or the grating moved between wavelengths? The Si drift points that way.
- Why is the Si line missing from 8 of the 12 spectra?
- Can you provide a cross-polarized spectrum or an angle series? Parallel-only data cannot separate E2g1 from 2LA(M) by polarization.

- **Si calibration:** the Si line drifts by about 1.1 cm⁻¹ across the series, which points to a spectrometer change.
- **Rejected components:** the 578.95 nm fit includes broad components at 532 and 566 cm⁻¹ whose errors exceed their heights. I treat them as background, not sample modes.

Open questions for you: the flake's exciton energy from PL or reflectance at 4 K, and whether the spectrometer was recalibrated between wavelengths.
